issues.description: Method RollerCoaster.getNumberOfLoopings(): the UML in the problem statement declares the attribute 'numberOfLoopings' as an int (problem_statement.md lines 26-28) and the exercise requires getters that return the attribute type. In the solution (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java) the getter is declared as public double getNumberOfLoopings() (signature at line 12) and returns (double) numberOfLoopings (cast at line 13). This creates a return-type mismatch between the UML/requirements (int) and the implemented getter (double), which can confuse students about the correct return type for the getter and lead to inconsistent implementations or failing expectations in tests that expect an int-returning getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter return the same type as the attribute declared in the UML. Change the method signature and implementation in RollerCoaster to: public int getNumberOfLoopings() { return numberOfLoopings; } (or, if a double was intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfLoopings as double). Prefer keeping attribute and getter types identical to avoid confusion.
